paper.title: Combinatorial Multi-Armed Bandit with General Reward Functions

settings.name_in_paper: CMAB with general reward functions (semi-bandit feedback)
unmapped: General nonlinear reward R(x,S) whose expectation may depend on the full outcome distributions (not only means)
Reward bounded in [0,M] (Assumption 2) and monotone in outcomes (Assumption 3)
Access via an alpha-approximation offline oracle for finite-support distributions (not a linear optimisation oracle; closest vocab chosen)
settings.definition_quote: We model a combinatorial multi-armed bandit (CMAB) problem as a tuple $(E, \calF, D, R)$, where $E = [m]$ is a set of $m$ (base) arms, $\calF \subseteq 2^{E}$ is a set of subsets of $E$, $D$ is a probability distribution over $[0, 1]^m$, and $R$ is a reward function defined on $[0, 1]^m \times \calF$.

settings.name_in_paper: CMAB with general reward functions, Lipschitz reward, known horizon
unmapped: General nonlinear reward, independent base arms, bounded by M, monotone, and Lipschitz with constant C in l1 norm (Assumptions 1-4)
Access via an alpha-approximation offline oracle
settings.definition_quote: Suppose the time horizon $T$ is known in advance. ... There exists $C>0$ such that for any $S \in \calF$ and any $x, x'\in [0, 1]^m$, we have $\left| R(x, S) - R(x', S) \right| \le C\|x_S - x_S'\|_1$

algorithms.name: Lazy-SDCB without knowing the time horizon

symbols.M_rew: upper bound M on the reward value
symbols.alpha_apx: approximation ratio alpha of the offline oracle
symbols.sum_EB_invDelta: sum over arms i in E_B (arms contained in some bad super arm) of 1/Delta_{i,min}, Delta_{i,min} = min gap of bad super arms containing i

source.label: thm:regret-bound-discrete
source.quote: A distribution-dependent upper bound on the $\alpha$-approximation regret of \texttt{SDCB} (Algorithm~\ref{alg:SDCB}) in $T$ rounds is $M^2 K  \sum_{i\in E_\bad} \frac{2136}{\Delta_{i, \min}}  \ln T  + \left( \frac{\pi^2}{3}  + 1 \right) \alpha Mm$

results.notes: Paper's K (max super arm size) mapped to canonical m; paper's m (base arms) is m_base. Regret is alpha-approximation regret defined via expected rewards r_D, hence pseudo-regret. SDCB uses ln t so no horizon needed. Compute depends on oracle; per-round time Theta(t).

symbols.alpha_apx: approximation ratio alpha of the offline oracle

results.notes: Paper's K -> m (super-arm size), paper's m -> m_base. alpha-approximation regret.

conditions: reward Lipschitz in l1 norm with constant C (L_lip)

source.label: thm:bound-know-T
source.quote: Suppose the time horizon $T$ is known in advance. Then the $\alpha$-approximation regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:Lazy-SDCB} in $T$ rounds is at most $93 M \sqrt{  mK T \ln T} + 2CK\sqrt T + \left( \frac{\pi^2}{3} + 1 \right)  \alpha Mm.$

results.notes: Paper's Lipschitz constant C mapped to L_lip; paper's K -> m; paper's m -> m_base. Per-round O(sqrt T) time and space excluding oracle.

symbols.M_rew: upper bound M on the reward value
symbols.alpha_apx: approximation ratio alpha of the offline oracle

conditions: reward Lipschitz in l1 norm with constant C (L_lip)

source.label: thm:bound-not-know-T
source.quote: For any time horizon $T \ge 2$, the $\alpha$-approximation regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:Lazy-SDCB-unknown-T} in $T$ rounds is at most $318M \sqrt{mKT  \ln T} + 7 CK \sqrt{T} + 10 \alpha Mm \ln T.$

results.notes: Algorithm does not need T (doubling trick), but recorded under setting s2 (which lists T as known) to share the Lipschitz assumption; learner does not actually need T.
